apidocs/SystemLibrary.Common.Framework.A.summary: Namespace SystemLibrary.Common.Framework.App Client Client is a class for all http(s) requests in your project Uses HttpClient and Polly behind the scenes for features such as reusing tcp connections, retry on 502 and 504 status codes, and optionally a request breaker for 7 seconds, if 25 error codes (404, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 505) occurs in a row useRetryPolicy: false, will retry once if request is a file request or GET or POST and status code is 502 or 504 Options: useRetryPolicy: True: same as 'false', but adds: retries one additional time on 502, 504 GET, POST - retries up to two times if response is null (timeout/no response) retries once on 401 GET, POST - retries once on 404 GET retries once on 500 GET, POST - retries once on 404, 500, 502 504 file request retries once on OPTION, PATCH, HEAD, CONNECT, TRACE ▼ Example ✕ You can simply "var client = new Client()" if you want and use the methods directly or inherit it and base all your integrations on it, sharing headers or other methods you would like. A simple class and HttpBinClient: class HttpBinResponse { public string Url { get; set; } } class HttpBinClient : Client { const string apiUrl = "http://httpbin.org"; public HttpBinClient() : base(useRetryPolicy: true) { } public HttpBinResponse Get() { return base.Get<HttpBinResponse>(apiUrl + "/get").Data; } } Running the above Client and Response in a UnitTest project as such: [TestMethod] public void Test() { var client = new HttpBinClient(); var response = client.Get(); Assert.IsTrue(response.Url.Contains("http")); //Visit: http://httpbin.org/get to see the actual value of 'url', then you know this Assert statement is true } Another example of using the Client directly: public void Test() { var client = new Client(); var response = client.Get<string>("http://httpbin.org/get"); Assert.IsTrue(response.Contains("http")); //Response is now the whole json (or any data actually as a string) text that the url: http://httpbin.org/get is returning } Another example returning HttpResponseMessage as is, for you to read the stream/content of the response yourself: public void Test() { var client = new Client(); var response = = client.Get<HttpResponseMessage>("http://httpbin.org/get"); var httpResponseMessage = response.Data; // httpResponseMessage now is ready to be read if you need to read it manually, as in: it's not a json/xml/serialization type of response, but maybe an Stream/Image you need to read... } ▼ Remarks ✕ Every client uses the Default configurations, which you can override in appsettings.json Most default configurations can again be overriden in the Clients constructor Each HttpClient pool behind the scenes, is based on scheme, url, port and timeout Each method also take an additional timeout parameter, a different timeout will target a different HttpClient Each underlying HttpClient is used for default 20 minutes, each TCP connection is maximum reused for 4 minutes and 55 seconds A 502 or 504 response on GET, POST or file request will always be retried once, cannot be turned off unless RetryTimeout is set to 0 in appSettings A new client wont neccesary create a new HttpClient, it might use from cache, it all depends on the url and params you pass in - In theory you could create just one client reusing towards any url you want But it's now up to you now: You want a new instance? documentation/apifilters.html.title: Api Filters | System Library Common Framework
documentation/apifilters.html.summary: Api Filters Description Attribute-based request filters for access control on controllers and actions. Built on top of BaseApiFilterAttribute which provides flexible value matching via exact string, wildcard, pipe-delimited or regex patterns. Features ApiTokenFilter: validates the api-token request header (or custom header name) OriginFilter: validates the Origin request header UserAgentFilter: validates the User-Agent request header — also blocks known bots, crawlers and spiders automatically when applied BaseApiFilterAttribute: base class for building custom filter attributes with built-in header value matching Behavior All filters use the same matching logic inherited from BaseApiFilterAttribute, evaluated in this order: null or * → allows all Exact string → case-sensitive match Pipe-delimited a|b → case-insensitive contains match against any part Wildcard *text* → case-insensitive starts/ends/contains match Regex ^pattern$ → compiled with RegexOptions.IgnoreCase — always case-insensitive On access denied, returns HTTP 403 with a JSON error body. Caveats Regex matching silently falls back to no-match if the pattern is invalid — no exception is thrown ApiTokenFilter defaults to api-token header name but accepts any custom header name UserAgentFilter blocks known bots and crawlers regardless of the match pattern — adding the attribute always enables bot blocking Filters return application/json on access denied — plain text and XML responses not yet supported Tip Inherit BaseApiFilterAttribute to build your own filter attributes — override OnActionExecuting and use RequestHasValidHeaderValue and OnAccessDenied for consistent behavior. Multiple attributes on the same controller are AND'd — every filter must pass. Use pipe-delimited values for OR logic, for instance: [ApiTokenFilter("token1|token2|token3")] Examples [ApiTokenFilter("SecretToken")] [OriginFilter("*.systemlibrary.com")] [UserAgentFilter("Chrome|Edg|Firefox")] public class OrderController : BaseApiController { } [ApiTokenFilter("^DEV-[A-Z0-9]{6}$")] public ActionResult SensitiveEndpoint() { }

documentation/application.html.title: Application | System Library Common Framework
documentation/application.html.summary: Application Description Entry point for starting and stopping the host. Wraps ASP.NET host setup into three startup approaches depending on how much control you need. Features Three startup APIs: Start, Build, and Extension — from zero-config to full control Hook support: IFrameworkHooks callbacks throughout the host lifecycle Async support: All startup methods have async variants Behavior Start API Simplest approach — framework manages the full host lifecycle: Application.Start<Hooks>(AppType.Web, options, AppHosting.Kestrel, urls); Build API Returns the host builder for additional configuration before running: var builder = Application.Build<Hooks>(AppType.Web, AppHosting.Kestrel, options, urls); var app = builder.Build(); app.Run(); Extension API Full control via extension methods directly on the host builder. IFrameworkHooks is not invoked in this mode: var builder = Host.CreateDefaultBuilder(args); builder.ConfigureFrameworkOptions(options); builder.ConfigureServices((context, services) => { services = services.AddFrameworkServices(AppType.Web); }); builder = builder.ConfigureWebHostDefaults(webBuilder => { webBuilder.UseKestrel(); webBuilder.Configure(app => { app.UseFrameworkBeginMiddlewares(AppType.Web); // ... app.UseFrameworkEndMiddlewares(AppType.Web); }); }); var app = builder.Build(); app.Run(); Stopping the host Application.HostStop(); // or await Application.HostStopAsync(); Caveats Calling Start or StartAsync twice throws InvalidOperationException — only one host instance is allowed IFrameworkHooks is not invoked when using the Framework Extension API Tip Use Application.Start for most applications. Use Application.Build if you need to configure the host after building. Use the Extension API if you're integrating into an existing host setup or you need full control. Modules work without registering middleware: Log, Cache, Client, Encryption, Json and Config AppSettings View all appsettings here

documentation/assemblies.html.title: Assemblies | System Library Common Framework
documentation/assemblies.html.summary: Assemblies Description Static class for scanning loaded assemblies and reading embedded resources. Features Whitelisted scanning: scans only your own assemblies — Microsoft, Newtonsoft, Serilog, NUnit and many others are excluded at startup, keeping scans fast Smart embedded resource lookup: pass just a filename or relative path, matches case-insensitively as fallback. Resource names are cached after first lookup per assembly Type scanning: find types by inheritance, interface implementation, or attribute decoration Caveats Type scanning is not cached internally — cache the result yourself if calling repeatedly Files must have build action set to Embedded Resource to be readable If multiple embedded files share the same filename, the first match wins Embedded resource max size is int.MaxValue bytes Tip Cache type scanning results at startup — scanning on every request is expensive.

documentation/cache.html.title: Cache | System Library Common Framework
documentation/cache.html.summary: Cache Description Application-level in-memory cache with built-in sharding for thread safety and scalability. Features Sharded cache: 8 cache containers out of the box Auto-generated key: includes namespace, class, method name, IsAuthenticated, user roles, and scoped variables of type string, int, DateTime, bool, or enum Behavior Duration: 3 minutes default CacheDuration: Predefined enum or any integer (seconds) Capacity: 320,000 items across 8 shards (40,000 per shard, configurable) Eviction: When full, 33% of items are removed via IMemoryCache eviction policy Fallback [Pro Tier]: Serves previously cached data when getItem() returns null or throws, for up to 3 minutes after primary expiration Skip Options skipWhenAuthenticated: Defaults to false skipWhenAdmin: Defaults to true, matches roles: Admin, Admins, Administrator, Administrators, WebAdmins, CmsAdmins (and lowercase variants) skipWhen: Custom condition, return true to skip Response cache Output cache Cache entire page or controller responses, with skip support for admins and authenticated users: // On a controller action: [OutputCache(Tags = [OutputCacheTag.SkipWhenAdmin])] public IActionResult Index() { ... } // On a razor page: @attribute [OutputCache(Tags = [OutputCacheTag.SkipWhenAdmin])] Available tags: OutputCacheTag.SkipWhenAdmin — skips cache for admin users OutputCacheTag.SkipWhenAuthenticated — skips cache for any authenticated user Warning SkipWhenAuthenticated and SkipWhenAdmin do not work on Razor Pages — controllers only. Caveats Auto-generated key is never user-specific — pass your own key containing userId/email to cache per user null is never cached Cache.Clear() may return default to concurrent callers during the brief reinitalization window Auto-generated key is capped at 2000 characters and 64 scoped variables — exceeding either logs an error Cache.Lock() is not a true lock — concurrent threads can still slip through Tip Pick duration by asking "what is the minimum time this data can be stale?" — always round down to the nearest CacheDuration value. documentation/client.html.title: Client | System Library Common Framework
documentation/client.html.summary: Client Description Class for making HTTP requests with built-in resilience, connection reuse and automatic retries. Uses HttpClient and Polly under the hood. Features All HTTP methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS — sync and async variants Connection reuse: underlying HttpClient cached per host, port, timeout, scheme, SSL and decompression settings — eliminates socket exhaustion Retry policy: configurable, see Behavior Circuit breaker [Pro Tier]: stops requests for 7 seconds after 25 consecutive errors on the same host + path Fluent API: call directly on any string URL via extension methods Behavior Defaults are read from appsettings and can be overridden per instance in the constructor. A new Client instance does not necessarily create a new underlying HttpClient — it reuses one from cache if scheme, host, port, timeout, SSL and decompression settings match. Retry policy disabled (default): Always retries once on 502, 504 for GET, POST and file requests Always retries once if remote host forcibly closes the connection These base retries cannot be disabled Retry policy enabled: All of the above, plus retries on 401, 404, 500 for GET/POST and file requests Up to two retries if response is null (timeout) 666ms delay between retries useRetryPolicy: false (default) Retries once on 502, 504 (GET, POST, file requests) useRetryPolicy: true Same as false, plus: Retries one extra time on 502, 504 (GET, POST) Retries twice if response is null (timeout/no response) Retries once on: 401 for GET, POST 404 for GET 500 for GET, POST 404, 500, 502, 504 for file requests 404, 502, 504 for OPTION, PATCH, HEAD, CONNECT, TRACE** Caveats DELETE and PUT are never retried 502 and 504 on GET, POST or file requests always retry at least once — set retryTimeout: 0 in appsettings to disable throwOnUnsuccessful defaults to false — errors are logged as warnings, not thrown ClientCertificate must include a private key or an exception is thrown Tip Inherit Client to build typed integration clients — share base URL, headers, and auth logic across all methods in one place. documentation/config.html.title: Config | System Library Common Framework
documentation/config.html.summary: Config Description Abstract base class for loading typed configuration from JSON, XML or .config files. Singleton per type — loaded once at first access, thread-safe. Features Auto-discovery: files are located by class name, searched in ~/, ~/Configs/ and ~/Configurations/ — file and class names are matched case-insensitively Transformations: environment-specific overrides via ClassName.Environment.json using ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT Auto-decryption: encrypted properties are decrypted at startup via naming convention or attribute Enum support: public enum fields are automatically mapped from configuration values appSettings support: config can also live as a named section inside appsettings.json User secrets support: set userSecretsId in appsettings to enable dotnet user-secrets for local development Behavior Config is loaded once on first access of Current and cached for the application lifetime. Transformations are applied on top of the base file — only properties defined in the transformation file are overridden. Decryption happens automatically at startup for properties matching either convention: Naming convention: TokenDecrypt decrypts the value of Token Attribute convention: [ConfigDecrypt("Token")] on any property name decrypts Token into it Values must be encrypted using string.Encrypt() — the parameterless version — so the same default key is used for both encryption and decryption. Caveats T cannot be a nested class Config file must exist and cannot be empty Decryption failures are logged as warnings and app continues Custom config files (non-appsettings) only support APP_ prefixed environment variables for overriding values — e.g. APP_PokemonConfig__Url=https://prod.api.com appsettings.json additionally supports ASPNETCORE_ and DOTNET_ prefixed variables Tip Store encrypted values safely in git — they are encrypted with a key only your application knows. See Encryption for details.

documentation/controllers.html.title: Controllers | System Library Common Framework
documentation/controllers.html.summary: Controllers Description The framework extends ASP.NET MVC with routing conventions, smart action selection, and a base API controller with built-in documentation endpoint. Features Auto-routing: controllers are routed automatically based on class name and namespace — no [Route] attributes needed BaseApiController: base class for all API controllers, adds /docs endpoint listing all actions and their parameters Short route: controllers suffixed with Api get both a full and short route — PokemonApiController resolves as both /api/pokemonapi/ and /api/pokemon/ Smart action selection: when multiple actions match a request, the one whose parameters best match the query string wins Behavior Routing conventions are applied automatically at startup — controllers inheriting Controller or BaseApiController get routes registered without any attributes. API routes are prefixed with /api/ and follow [controller]/[action] pattern. Namespace segments beyond the root are included in the path: MyApp.Api.Admin.UserApiController → /api/admin/userapi/ and /api/admin/user/ Action selection resolves ambiguity when multiple overloads exist — if query string parameters match an action's parameter names, that action wins. If no query string exists, the parameterless action wins. Caveats Controllers with an explicit [Route] attribute are excluded from auto-routing conventions Controllers with [ApiController] attribute are excluded from auto-routing conventions Tip Inherit BaseApiController for all your APIs to get the free /docs endpoint.

documentation/dispatch.html.title: Dispatch | System Library Common Framework
documentation/dispatch.html.summary: Dispatch Description Static helpers for running functions in parallel or as fire-and-forget background tasks. Features Dispatch.Parallel<T>(): runs multiple functions in parallel, collects and returns results Dispatch.Parallel(): runs multiple actions in parallel, no return value Dispatch.FireAndForget(): runs actions in background threads — non-blocking, caller never waits Behavior Parallel uses Parallel.ForEach with max degree of parallelism set to ProcessorCount / 4 — intentionally conservative to avoid starving the web server thread pool. Default timeout is 30 seconds — configurable per call. If timeout is hit, collected results so far are returned and an error is logged. Exceptions inside individual functions are caught, logged and skipped — remaining functions continue. FireAndForget wraps each action in Task.Run — each action runs independently on the thread pool. Exceptions are caught and passed to the optional onError callback. If no callback is provided exceptions are silently swallowed. Caveats Parallel result order is not guaranteed — ConcurrentBag is unordered Parallel null return values are silently skipped — default(T) is added on exception FireAndForget actions run until completion or app shutdown — no cancellation support FireAndForget without onError callback swallows all exceptions silently Tip Use Parallel for independent IO calls that can run simultaneously — fetching from multiple APIs, loading multiple config files. Use FireAndForget for work that must not block the caller — sending emails, writing audit logs. !!SKIP!!

documentation/encryption.html.title: Encryption | System Library Common Framework
documentation/encryption.html.summary: Encryption Description Extension methods for encrypting and decrypting strings and byte arrays using AES CBC, AES GCM, RSA, or the ASP.NET Data Protection key ring. All methods are available directly on string and byte[]. Features AES CBC: symmetric encryption, default algorithm, IV prepended to output AES GCM: symmetric encryption with authentication tag, tamper-evident RSA: asymmetric encryption using auto-generated or custom PEM key files Key Ring: wraps ASP.NET Data Protection API — useful for short-lived tokens and cookies Auto key discovery: key file is located automatically by scanning parent directories — no configuration required in most cases Behavior Key resolution order at startup: CLI argument --slcf-encryption-key=yourkey Environment variable SLCF_ENCRYPTION_KEY Key file named enc-*.key in configured or auto-discovered directory Falls back to default key ABCD... The resolved key is hashed together with 'app:name' to produce a final 32-byte AES key, meaning the same raw key produces different keys across different app names. Key file discovery scans parent directories upward from the app root (up to 10 levels) looking for enc-*.key, pem.pub and pem.priv files. If multiple .key files exist the oldest is used — allowing key rotation without breaking existing encrypted values. RSA key files are auto-generated on first use if none exist in the configured directory. Public key (.pub) is used for encryption, private key (.priv) for decryption. Decryption caching: frequently decrypted short values (under 255 chars) are cached in memory — up to 64 entries per algorithm — to avoid repeated decryption overhead. Key Ring uses the app name as the protection purpose — requires app:name to be set in appsettings in production or it throws. Caveats Default fallback key ABC... is shared across all framework users — never use it in production AES CBC key must be 16, 24 or 32 bytes — throws otherwise AES GCM IV must be 12 bytes, AES CBC IV must be 16 bytes — throws otherwise RSA requires a private key for decryption — throws if private key is missing Key Ring encrypted values cannot be decrypted across applications or after key ring rotation unless persistence is configured Encrypted values in config files may trigger GitHub secret scanning — add config paths to .github/secret_scanning.yml to suppress Tip Store your enc-*.key file outside the repository as the filename after enc- is your encryption password. For stronger keys with unrestricted characters, pass the key via CLI argument --slcf-encryption-key= or environment variable SLCF_ENCRYPTION_KEY. Use minimum 32 characters mixing uppercase, lowercase, digits and symbols as the key — the longer and more random the better. AppSettings View all appsettings here

documentation/enum.html.title: Enum | System Library Common Framework
documentation/enum.html.summary: Enum Description Extensions and attributes for enriching enums with metadata, enabling conversion between enum keys, custom text and custom values — with full support in JSON serialization. Features EnumText attribute: attach a custom text to any enum key EnumValue attribute: attach a custom value (any type) to any enum key ToText(): returns EnumText value or falls back to key name as string ToValue(): returns EnumValue value or falls back to key name as string GetEnumText(): returns EnumText value or null if attribute not present GetEnumValue(): returns EnumValue value or null if attribute not present ToEnum(): converts string to enum key — matches key name, EnumValue or EnumText (case insensitive) IsAny(): checks if enum matches any in a list EnumExtensions<T>: static helpers to get all keys, enums or values from an enum type Model binding: ToEnum() is registered globally via TypeDescriptor — ASP.NET model binding automatically uses EnumValue and EnumText matching for query strings, form posts and route values Behavior ToEnum() matching priority: Direct key name match (case insensitive) EnumValue attribute match (case insensitive) EnumText attribute match (case insensitive) Returns first key in enum (default) if no match ToValue() strips leading underscore from keys formatted as _0something — allowing numeric-prefixed enum keys that are invalid in C# without the underscore prefix. JSON serialization via string.Json() respects both EnumValue and EnumText attributes during deserialization and serialization. TypeDescriptor — all ASP.NET model binding automatically uses EnumValue and EnumText attribute matching when converting strings to enums, including query strings, form posts and route values. Caveats GetEnumText() and GetEnumValue() return null if attribute is not present — use ToText() / ToValue() if you want a fallback to key name EnumExtensions<T> uses static methods instead of extension methods due to C# generic type constraints Tip Use EnumValue for machine-readable identifiers (IDs, codes, symbols) and EnumText for human-readable display strings — they serve different purposes and can both be applied to the same key.

documentation/environmentconfig.html.title: EnvironmentConfig | System Library Common Framework
documentation/environmentconfig.html.summary: EnvironmentConfig Description Provides environment detection and configuration based on ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT. Inherits from Config<T> — supports the same file discovery, transformations and decryption. Features Environment detection: IsDevelopment, IsTest, IsProd static flags available anywhere Environment name: reads from ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT across all hosting models — IIS, IISExpress, Kestrel, Test Explorer, CLI Typed environment enum: inherit EnvironmentConfig<T, TEnum> to map environment name to your own enum ContentRootPath: static path to the application root folder Behavior IsDevelopment is true when neither IsProd nor IsTest is true — it's the fallback, not an explicit check. IsTest covers a broad range of non-production, non-development environments: AT, Integration, PreProd, PreProduction, QA, Sandbox, Stage, Staging, Test, UAT, UnitTest, CI, ContinuousIntegration, Build IsProd matches only Prod and Production. Environment name resolution priority varies by hosting model but generally follows: environmentConfig.json transformation file for current environment environmentConfig.json name property ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT from mstest.runsettings, web.config, launchSettings.json or Windows environment variables Falls back to "" — never null Caveats IsDevelopment returns true if environment is unset or unrecognized — safe default but worth being aware of Inherit EnvironmentConfig<YourClass, YourEnum> if you need additional properties beyond Name and EnvironmentType ContentRootPath strips /bin/ and /lib/ path segments automatically — returns the project root, not the build output folder Tip Use EnvironmentConfig.IsProd instead of string.Equals(env, "Production") — it handles both Prod and Production and is available globally without injection.

documentation/extensions.html.title: Extensions | System Library Common Framework
documentation/extensions.html.summary: Extensions Description A lof of common extensions for any application, heres a sample list of the most useful ones: Features StringExtensions: Is() and IsNot() ToDateTime() ToDate() ToMd5() ToBase64() and FromBase64() Compress() and Decompress() Obfuscate() and Unobfuscate() ToPascalCase() and toCamelCase() MaxLength() GetSampledKey() Encrypt() and Decrypt() ConcurrentDictionaryExtensions: Cache() StringBuilderExtensions: Is() and IsNot() IndexOf() EndsWith() GetSampledKey() IListExtensions: Is() and IsNot() Behavior All extension methods should work out of the box and most never throws.

documentation/frameworkoptions.html.title: FrameworkOptions | System Library Common Framework
documentation/frameworkoptions.html.summary: FrameworkOptions Description Controls which services and middleware are registered at startup. Passed to Application.Start, Application.Build or the extension API. Features All options default to sensible values — only override what you need. Middleware toggles: UseAuthentication — default true UseAuthorization — default true UseForwardedHeaders — default true UseHttpsRedirection — default false UseHsts — default false UseOutputCache — default true UseGzipResponseCompression — default true UseBrotliResponseCompression — default false UseDeveloperPage — default true UseStatusCodeLogger — default true UseStaticFilePolicy — default true UseSecurityPolicy — default true UseResponseCaching — default true UseDataProtectionPolicy — default false Static files: StaticFilesClientCacheSeconds — default 604800 (7 days) StaticRequestPaths — custom static file root paths Views: ViewLocations — custom view location formats ViewLocationExpander — custom IViewLocationExpander implementation ApplicationParts — additional assemblies scanned for controllers Behavior UseSecurityPolicy only adds security headers in production — non-production environments allow all content freely to simplify local development and testing. UseDataProtectionPolicy generates a single key file in the parent of ContentRoot valid for 100 years — copy it to all environments and gitignore it. Required for EncryptUsingKeyRing and DecryptUsingKeyRing and for cookie encryption across multiple instances. Caveats UseDataProtectionPolicy is false by default — keys are stored in-memory only, meaning auth cookies are lost on app restart and won't work across multiple instances. Enable it to persist keys to disk. UseHsts and UseHttpsRedirection are both false by default — enable only if your hosting environment does not handle HTTPS termination upstream StaticRequestPaths requires UseStaticFilePolicy to be true Tip Enable UseDataProtectionPolicy in production if you use cookie authentication or run multiple instances — otherwise users will be logged out on every restart. Copy the generated key file to all environments and gitignore it. Usage var options = new FrameworkOptions(); Application.Start<Hooks>(AppType.Web, options, AppHosting.Kestrel);

documentation/hooks.html.title: Hooks | System Library Common Framework
documentation/hooks.html.summary: Hooks Description Callbacks for hooking into framework startup — register services, extend the middleware pipeline and react to host events. Features Service registration: OnConfigureServices — register your own services alongside framework services Pipeline hooks: tap into the request pipeline at specific points Host lifecycle hooks: react to host building, built and started events Behavior Service hook: OnConfigureServices(services, env) → called during service registration Pipeline hooks (called per branch — Web, Static, Api): OnPipelineBegin → after rate limiter and block middleware, before all others OnBeforeEndpoints → called before controllers and routes are mapped OnAfterEndpoints → called after controllers and routes are mapped — add extra endpoints here OnPipelineEnd → after pipeline is fully built Host lifecycle hooks: OnHostBuilding → configure host (logging, DI, etc.) OnHostBuilt → read final host configuration OnHostStarted → app is live — perform warmup, seed data, start background jobs Caveats All hook methods have default empty implementations — only override what you need IFrameworkHooks is not invoked when using the Framework Extension API — use extension methods directly in that case OnAuthorization requires both UseAuthentication and UseAuthorization to be true in FrameworkOptions Tip Use OnHostStarted for warmup tasks like pre-loading cache or seeding data — the host is fully live at that point and all services are available.

documentation/httpcontextinstance.html.title: HttpContextInstance | System Library Common Framework
documentation/httpcontextinstance.html.summary: HttpContextInstance Description Global thread-safe access to the current HttpContext — the .NET Framework HttpContext.Current pattern brought back for ASP.NET Core. Features HttpContextInstance.Current: returns the current HttpContext from anywhere without injection Behavior var context = HttpContextInstance.Current; var path = context.Request?.Path; Caveats If no active HTTP context exists, returns a default HttpContext with an empty ClaimsPrincipal and the framework service provider — never returns null. Returns a default empty context (not null) outside of HTTP requests — console apps, background jobs, unit tests Requires AddFrameworkServices() to be called at startup — registered automatically by the framework Tip Use HttpContextInstance.Current in static helpers and extension methods where injection is not available.

documentation/json.html.title: Json | System Library Common Framework
documentation/json.html.summary: Json Description Extension methods for serializing and deserializing JSON on string and object, with built-in custom converters and JSON attribute support. Features object.Json(): serialize to JSON string, optional camelCase string.Json<T>(): deserialize JSON string to T string.JsonFind<T>(): extract and deserialize a specific property — supports path notation root/child/leaf JsonEncrypt: transparently encrypts/decrypts a property during serialization JsonObfuscate: transparently obfuscates/deobfuscates a property during serialization JsonCompress: transparently compresses/decompresses a property during serialization Behavior Built-in converters handle common edge cases — tolerant parsing of string, int, long, DateTime, DateTimeOffset, Guid, Uri and Enum. Non-serializable types (Exception, Thread, Stream etc) are silently skipped. Circular references are ignored. JsonFind<T> searches depth-first — for List<T> automatically appends s to the type name when no path is specified. Caveats JsonFind throws if a node in a specified path is not found dynamic deserialization bypasses custom converters — dates and enums return as raw strings JsonSerializerOptions is not a singleton — recreated per call for thread safety Tip Use JsonFind<T> when consuming large third-party API responses — extract only what you need without deserializing the entire payload.

documentation/log.html.title: Log | System Library Common Framework
documentation/log.html.summary: Log Description Global static logging available anywhere without injection. Messages are queued and written on a background thread — main thread is never blocked. Supports file, stdout/stderr and custom writers. Features Global access: Log.Error(), Log.Warning(), Log.Information(), Log.Debug(), Log.Trace(), Log.Critical(), Log.Dump() — no injection needed Auto-enrichment: optionally appends URL, query string, browser name, correlation ID and authenticated state to each message Multiple formats: Text, JSON or HTML output Log forwarding: forward framework logs to stdout/stderr, or forward stdout/stderr into your ILogWriter File writer: built-in fallback file writer with file size limit Flush on shutdown: queue is drained before app exits Behavior Log.Dump() bypasses the queue and rate limiter — written immediately and directly. Use for debugging only. Log.Debug() and Log.Dump() skip URL, browser and stack trace enrichment for performance. Log forwarding modes: Default → your ILogWriter receives all log calls, stdout/stderr untouched LogToStd → all log calls go to stdout/stderr with ANSI color support StdToLog → stdout/stderr is forwarded into your ILogWriter If no ILogWriter is registered, falls back to file writer at %HomeDrive%/Logs/Dump.log. Correlation ID is auto-generated per request if not already present in HttpContext.Items. Caveats Log.Dump() should not be used in production — no rate limiting, no queuing, direct write File writer has no log rotation Rate limited: max 400 messages per 4ms interval, discards silently and logs one warning per overflow Tip Implement ILogWriter and register it as a singleton to send logs to Datadog, Application Insights or any other sink — the framework handles all enrichment and formatting before calling Write(). documentation/metrics.html.title: Metrics | System Library Common Framework
documentation/metrics.html.summary: Metrics Description Prometheus-based metrics with a built-in pie chart UI. Increment counters anywhere in your code and view them as charts at a dedicated endpoint — no external tools required. Features Metric.Inc(label, segment): increment a counter from anywhere in code Built-in UI: pie charts rendered at /metrics/ui Multi-node support: UI fetches metrics from all running instances simultaneously Auto-coloring: segment names like error, success, timeout get meaningful colors automatically Custom colors and ordering: configure per-metric via MetricCharts Behavior Two endpoints are registered automatically when metrics are enabled: /metrics → raw Prometheus text format /metrics/ui → pie chart dashboard (Pro Tier) UI is cached for 20 seconds — refreshes automatically on next request after expiry. Multi-node fetching makes 7 parallel requests to the metrics endpoint — aggregates results across load balanced instances. Auto-color mapping based on segment name: error, fail, crash, 500, 502 → red success, hit, ok, 200, 201 → green warn, notfound, 404 → orange timeout, unauthorized, 401 → light red circuit, broken, 503 → dark red Caveats Metrics UI requires Pro Tier license Metric.Inc() is a no-op if metrics are disabled — zero overhead Multi-node fetching assumes all instances are reachable on the same host/port — configure metricUIUrl in appsettings if behind a proxy Default Prometheus metrics are suppressed — only framework and consumer metrics are shown Tip Use label for the category and segment for the outcome: Metric.Inc("checkout", "success"); Metric.Inc("checkout", "timeout"); Metric.Inc("cache", "hit"); Metric.Inc("cache","miss"); Most common segments are auto-colored — success is green, timeout is red, no configuration needed. documentation/security.html.title: Security | System Library Common Framework
documentation/security.html.summary: Security Description The framework adds a baseline of security behaviors out of the box — not a substitute for proper security testing, but a reasonable starting point. Features Request blocking: Requests to sensitive paths and file extensions are blocked automatically — see Static Files for the full list. Security headers (production only): X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff — all responses Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=2592000; includeSubDomains — always sent, browsers respect it only over HTTPS Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin — on non-file requests Content-Security-Policy — web responses only: All sources allowed (default-src *) Plugin embedding blocked (object-src 'none') Base URI restricted to same origin (base-uri 'self') Iframing restricted to your domain and subdomains (frame-ancestors) Bot and crawler blocking: UserAgentFilter attribute blocks known bots and crawlers when applied to a controller or action. Encryption: AES CBC, AES GCM and RSA available out of the box — see Encryption. What the framework does NOT do Penetration testing Vulnerability scanning OWASP compliance verification Security auditing Whitelist or validate scripts running on your site as CSP is set to default-src * Caveats Security headers are only added in production — other environments allow all content freely to simplify local development and testing TODO: And should also be added to preproduction - so we have an environment equal to production

documentation/services.html.title: Services | System Library Common Framework
documentation/services.html.summary: Services Description Global service locator providing access to the configured IServiceProvider anywhere in the application — without injection. Features Services.Get<T>(): resolve any registered service globally Behavior var accessor = Services.Get<IHttpContextAccessor>(); var context = accessor?.HttpContext; Services.Current is initialized twice: At bootstrap with a minimal default provider (HttpContextAccessor, DataProtection, etc.) Overwritten when UseFrameworkBeginMiddleware is invoked This ensures framework internals work even before the full DI container is available. Caveats Returns null if service is not registered — no exception thrown Avoid using Services.Get<T>() in constructors during startup — the full provider may not be initialized yet This is a service locator — use constructor injection where possible, reserve this for places where injection is not available (static classes, extension methods, filters) Tip Use Services.Get<T>() in static contexts where DI injection is not possible — global helpers, static extensions, or framework internals. For regular classes prefer constructor injection.

documentation/shardeddicstionary.html.title: ShardedDictionary | System Library Common Framework
documentation/shardeddicstionary.html.summary: ShardedDictionary Description A thread-safe generic dictionary that distributes keys across 4 shards to reduce lock contention and improve throughput under concurrent load. Features Sharded storage: 4 internal ConcurrentDictionary shards — keys distributed by hash Auto-clear: each shard clears itself when it reaches capacity — no manual management needed Cache helper: Cache(key, getItem) returns existing value or creates and stores a new one Standard API: TryAdd, TryGetValue, TryRemove, ContainsKey, TryUpdate, Clear, Count, Keys Behavior Shard is selected by key.GetHashCode() & 3 — O(1) shard lookup. When a shard exceeds its capacity (maxItemCount / 4), the entire shard is cleared before adding the new item. This is a hard clear — not LRU, not eviction — all items in that shard are lost. Default total capacity is 100,000 items (25,000 per shard). Cache() is a get-or-create helper — if key exists returns it, otherwise calls getItem(), stores and returns result. Used extensively inside the framework for reflection caching. Caveats Shard clear is all-or-nothing — when capacity is hit, entire shard is wiped, not just oldest entries Count property iterates all 4 shards — slightly expensive, avoid in tight loops Keys property yields across all shards — not a snapshot, concurrent modifications may affect iteration ClearLock is a static object — shared across ALL ShardedDictionary instances, potential contention Tip Use Cache() instead of TryGetValue + TryAdd — it handles the get-or-create pattern atomically per shard.

documentation/staticfiles.html.title: StaticFiles | System Library Common Framework
documentation/staticfiles.html.summary: StaticFiles Description Serves static files from well-known asset folders with sensible defaults — cache headers, compression and unknown file type support out of the box. Features Auto-discovery: serves files from wwwroot, public, static, dist, frontend, assets, files automatically Client-side caching: Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, immutable applied to all static files by default (7 days) Unknown file types: served without restriction — no file extension whitelist Compression: HTTPS compression enabled by default Behavior Static files are served from two sources: WebRootPath (wwwroot) — standard ASP.NET web root, served at / Asset folders — served at their folder name as path segment: ~/public/ → /public/ ~/static/ → /static/ ~/dist/ → /dist/ ~/frontend/ → /frontend/ ~/assets/ → /assets/ ~/files/ → /files/ Only GET and HEAD requests are handled — all other methods pass through to the next middleware. Cache header is only added if not already present — consumers can override per file or route. Security Certain paths and file extensions are blocked automatically — returns 403 Forbidden: Blocked paths: /app_data/ /properties/ /configs/ /configurations/ /bin/ /obj/ appsettings.* Blocked extensions: .exe .dll .iso .msi .ps1 .cmd .sh .bash .vbs .dmg .config .env .ini .key .pem .cshtml .cs .sql .mdf .bat .jar .php .py .pl .rb .go .vb .hta .bak .db .pfx .crt This runs before static file serving — blocked requests never reach the file system. Caveats UseStaticFilePolicy must be true in FrameworkOptions — enabled by default If WebRootPath is set but folder does not exist — logs a warning and continues Cache duration is controlled by StaticFilesClientCacheSeconds in FrameworkOptions — default 604800 (7 days) Tip Place your CSS, JS and images in ~/wwwroot or any of the auto-discovered asset folders — no configuration needed. Files are immediately available at their path.

documentation/systemtype.html.title: SystemType | System Library Common Framework
documentation/systemtype.html.summary: SystemType Description Static class providing pre-cached Type instances for common .NET types. Avoids repeated typeof() calls throughout the framework and in consumer code. Features Covers all common types: Primitives: string, int, long, short, bool, char, byte, double, decimal, float, uint, ulong, ushort Dates: DateTime, DateTimeOffset, TimeSpan — including nullable variants Collections: IList, ICollection, IDictionary, List<>, Dictionary<,> — generic and non-generic Other: Guid, Uri, object, ExpandoObject, Delegate, Tuple, BigInteger, Half Attributes: EnumValueAttribute, EnumTextAttribute Arrays: byte[], int[] Behavior All fields are static and initialized once at class load — zero overhead after first access. Caveats Fields are public static not readonly — technically mutable, but should never be reassigned Tip Use SystemType.IntType instead of typeof(int) in hot paths — the cached instance avoids repeated type resolution overhead. Particularly useful in reflection-heavy code called frequently. Usage if(type == SystemType.IntType) { ... }

documentation/views.html.title: Views | System Library Common Framework
documentation/views.html.summary: Views Description The framework extends ASP.NET view discovery to support feature-folder structure — controllers and their views can live in the same folder anywhere in the project. Features Feature folder support: views are discovered next to their controllers Auto namespace discovery: controller namespaces are automatically registered as view search paths at startup Custom view locations: add extra view paths via FrameworkOptions.ViewLocations Custom expander: pass your own IViewLocationExpander via FrameworkOptions.ViewLocationExpander Behavior The framework registers these view search paths automatically: /{controller}/{view}.cshtml /{namespaceSegment}/{controller}/{view}.cshtml /{namespaceSegment}/{controller}/{controller}.cshtml /{namespaceSegment}/{controller}/Views/{view}.cshtml /{namespaceSegment}/Views/Shared/{controller}/{view}.cshtml Namespace segments of discovered controllers are also added as view search paths — so a controller in MyApp.Content.Home namespace automatically registers Content/Home as a valid view root. Custom locations from FrameworkOptions are appended after the built-in paths — built-in paths always take priority. Caveats Built-in view paths take priority View namespace discovery runs once on first request — not at startup ApplicationParts must be set in FrameworkOptions if controllers live in external assemblies Custom ViewLocationExpander runs alongside the built-in expander — both are active simultaneously Tip Organise your project as feature folders — keep HomeController.cs and Index.cshtml in the same ~/Content/Home/ folder. No configuration needed, the framework discovers them automatically.

tutorial/index.html.title: Tutorial | System Library Common Framework
tutorial/index.html.summary:
Tutorial Duration: 30 minutes This tutorial takes you from a basic installation to a working application using the framework which gets you hand on experience with the frameworks most commonly used modules. Each chapter builds on the previous one. Prerequisite You've followed the Installation instructions You have an appsettings.json file with at least an app name: { "systemLibraryCommonFramework": { "app": { "name": "company_unique_appname" } } } Chapter 1: Setup Choose one of the four startup approaches depending on how much control you need. Four different Programs.cs: Application Start Minimal API (1) Application.Start(); Application Start API (2) var options = new FrameworkOptions(); Application.Start(AppType.Web, options, AppHosting.Kestrel); public class Hooks : IFrameworkHooks { public void OnConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services, EnvironmentType env) { } } Application Build API (3) var options = new FrameworkOptions(); var urls = new[] { "http://localhost:5010" }; var builder = Application.Build(AppType.Web, AppHosting.Kestrel, options, urls); var app = builder.Build(); app.Run(); public class Hooks : IFrameworkHooks { public void OnConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services, EnvironmentType env) { } } Framework Extension API (4) Warning IFrameworkHooks is not invoked when using the Framework Extension API, as this gives you full control as now you invoke only extension methods. var options = new FrameworkOptions(); var builder = Host.CreateDefaultBuilder(args); builder.ConfigureFrameworkOptions(options); builder.ConfigureServices((context, services) => { services = services.AddFrameworkServices(AppType.Web); }); builder = builder.ConfigureWebHostDefaults(webBuilder => { webBuilder.UseKestrel(); webBuilder.Configure(app => { app.UseFrameworkBeginMiddlewares(AppType.Web); app.UseFrameworkEndMiddlewares(AppType.Web); }); }); var app = builder.Build(); app.Run(); Chapter 2: Configuration There are three ways to configure the framework: appsettings.json (1) appsettings.json for global module settings which might differ per environment, to support transformations. { "systemLibraryCommonFramework": { "app": { "name": "company_public_website" } } } FrameworkOptions (2) Controls which services and middleware are registered on startup. var options = new FrameworkOptions { UseDeveloperPage = true, UseHttpsRedirection = false }; Public framework interfaces (3) Some framework behaviors can be replaced by implementing and registering an interface in your DI container. Example: ILogWriter – implement it to control where log messages are written: services.AddSingleton(); Chapter 3: Log Log is globally available in the global namespace, simply write anywhere: Log.Error(any); Log.Warning(any); Messages are queued and written on a background thread. appsettings.json: { "systemLibraryCommonFramework": { "log": { "level": "Warning", // optional, defaults to Logging:LogLevel:Default "format": "Text" } } } ILogWriter Implement the interface to control where messages go, without an implementation all log methods goes to stderr and stdout by default. public class LogWriter : ILogWriter { public void Write(LogLevel level, string message) { Console.WriteLine(message); } } Register it as a singleton: public class Hooks : IFrameworkHooks { public void OnConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services, EnvironmentType env) { services.AddSingleton(); } } Chapter 4: Controllers and Views Setup controller and a matching view as a feature/module component. We will put controller and view in the same folder. Add ~/Content/Home/HomeController.cs: public class HomeController : Controller { public IActionResult Index() { Log.Error("Hello home controller " + DateTime.Now); object model = "Hello world " + DateTime.Now; return View(model); } } Add ~/Content/Home/Index.cshtml @model object

Title: @Model.ToString()

Run your application and visit http://localhost:5010/ http://localhost:5010/Home Warning If you already have a Index view in ~/Pages/Index.cshtml then razor pages will pick up that instead. Chapter 5: Static Files All asset folders can be used as a root of the website to host assets (files). Let's create the folder ~/wwwroot and add a image.png inside: ~/wwwroot/image.png This image is now available on url http://localhost:5010/image.png Note that static files can be placed in any asset folders named: "public", "static", "dist", "frontend", "assets", "files", "public", "assets", "files" and last and probably most default one: "wwwroot" All asset folders host files with a 7 days cache on client side by default. Chapter 6: Config Load typed configuration from json, xml or config files automatically. Note: files and classes are not case sensitive. Example Add ~/Configs/pokemonConfig.json: { "url": "", "cacheDuration": 10 } And add transformation ~/Configs/PokemonConfig.Development.json: { "url": "https://localhost:5010/api", "cacheDuration": 4 } Add ~/Configs/PokemonConfig.cs: public class PokemonConfig : Config { public string Url { get; set; } public int CacheDuration { get; set; } } Usage var url = PokemonConfig.Current.Url; Chapter 7: Api Controllers Add ~/Api/PokemonApiController.cs public class PokemonApiController : BaseApiController { public IActionResult Pikachu() { return Json("Hello Pikachu"); } } Run your application, visit: http://localhost:5010/api/pokemonapi/pikachu http://localhost:5010/api/pokemonapi/docs Classes inheriting BaseApiController routes are prefixed with /api/. The Controller suffix is always stripped, and the Api suffix is optional, so both /api/pokemon/ and /api/pokemonapi/ resolve to the same controller. Chapter 8: Client Use the Client for any HTTP request. public class PokemonApiController : BaseApiController { public IActionResult Pikachu() { var url = PokemonConfig.Current.Url + "/pokemon/pikachu" var client = new Client(); var response = client.Get(url); // Optionally: use the client's fluent api //var name = url.GetRequest().Data?.name; var name = response.Data?.name; return Json("Hello " + name); } } Chapter 9: Cache Three cache types available depending on your use case, in this tutorial we just go over the in-memory cache. In-memory cache Wraps any result in memory. Skip cache for admins by default. Navigate to ~/Api/PokemonApiController.cs public IActionResult Pikachu() { var duration = PokemonConfig.Current.CacheDuration; if(duration == 0) { duration = (int)CacheDuration.XS; } var name = Cache.Get(() => { var client = new Client(); var apiUrl = PokemonConfig.Current.Url; var response = client.Get(apiUrl + "/pokemon/pikachu"); var name = response.Data?.name + " " + DateTime.Now.Second; return name; }, duration); return Json("Hello " + name); } Chapter 10: Modules and Extensions The framework includes many additional modules, classes, and extensions. For more in-depth information, see the framework documentation. Here are some worth highlighting: Modules: Assemblies // read embedded resources Methods // run async or in parallel Metrics // count function calls and view its pie chart out of the box Extensions: ToBase64, FromBase64 ToBase62, FromBase62 Encrypt, Decrypt, ToServerPath, Json, PartialJson, Xml, Is, IsNot, ToMd5, ToSha256, GetFingerprint, GetSampledKey, ToEnumValue, ToEnumText, ToEnum ToDateTime, ToDateTimeOffset, Compress, Decompress Types: EnumValue-attribute // add metadata to Enum Keys, retrieve through ToEnumValue() EnumText-attribute // add metadata to Enum Keys, retrieve through ToEnumText() SystemType // pre-made 'typeof' calls EnvironmentConfig.Current // built-in to figure out the env name and more Documentations Documentation — behavior, features and caveats per module API Documentation — public API with signatures, summaries and examples Suggestions email: support@systemlibrary.com
